hook: His sailboat was going down 25 miles out on the lake.
narration: His sailboat was going down, twenty-five miles off Grand Haven, Michigan.
The bow was already under, and the mast was leaning toward the water.
A Coast Guard boat crew from Station Grand Haven came alongside.
That orange collar on the response boat is a foam fender, built to take hits from other hulls.
[short pause] He went into the water, and the crew hauled him aboard.
Behind them, the sailboat kept going down.
outcome: The sailor was safe, and his boat sank in three hundred feet of water.
title: Sailboat sinking 25 miles off Michigan
question_comment: Would you have stayed with the boat or gone into the water?

description:
Crews from Coast Guard Station Grand Haven and Air Station Traverse City rescued a man from a sinking sailboat 25 miles off Grand Haven, Michigan, on May 27, 2024. The sailboat sank in 300 feet of water.
